grimoire.title: Level-5 Phantom
grimoire.text: Hostile, mobile, intelligent. Drops ambient temperature below zero and pushes EMF past 90 mG. Pins civilians behind obstacles. Disrupts electrical and network systems. Weak to salt, UV and banishment.

grimoire.title: Banishment rite (Ordo Loft)
grimoire.text: Full exorcism protocol. Only after civilians are clear of the contact zone; takes 6-8 minutes; high success against level-5 phantoms once contained.

grimoire.title: Human crowd (not an entity)
grimoire.text: High motion events with normal EMF (<10 mG) and normal temperature are people, not ghosts. Classic false alarm. Do not escalate; observe.

grimoire.title: UV lantern array
grimoire.text: Ultraviolet flood at 365nm destabilises ectoplasmic manifestations and drops EMF readings. Best against level-4+ phantoms in enclosed sectors such as catering bays.

grimoire.title: Residual echo
grimoire.text: A replaying imprint. Low confidence sightings, single witness, mild EMF (30-50 mG). Non-hostile. Doctrine: observe, do not engage.

grimoire.title: Spectral decoy beacon
grimoire.text: Emits a warm EMF signature to lure an entity away from pinned civilians toward an isolated zone.

snippets: About 90 PG&E customers in the Castro District were still without power on Saturday after a small outage struck a stretch of Market Street on Friday.

# Power outage affects part of SF's Market Street after equipment damage
#### By Bay City News • Published July 4, 2026 • Updated on July 4, 2026 at 12:00 pm
About 90 Pacific Gas and Electric customers in San Francisco's Castro District were still without power on Saturday after a small outage struck a stretch of Market Street on Friday.

Traffic signals could be inoperable in the outage area, which included most of the 2200 block of Market Street and the blocks between Noe and Sanchez streets and from 15th to 16th streets, according to the San Francisco Department of Emergency Management.

evidence.title: Massive San Francisco power outage darkened entire neighborhoods for hours
evidence.description: Roughly 21,000 San Francisco households and businesses remain without power following a massive PG&E outage that brought a portion of the city to a halt.
snippets:
# Massive San Francisco power outage darkened entire neighborhoods for hours
Miles Barrett, assistant designer at Industry of All Nations, reads “Red Rising” by Pierce Brown by candlelight during a power outage in San Francisco on Saturday. The store had to close early due to a power outage.

Yalonda M. James/S.F. Chronicle

Ryan Sicat, store manager of Industry of All Nations, stands inside the store in San Francisco during Saturday’s power outage.

Ryan Sicat, store manager of Industry of All Nations, stands inside the store in San Francisco during Saturday’s power outage.

Yalonda M. James/S.F. Chronicle

**S.F. outage update:** More than 48 hours later, some parts of the city are still without power

A series of widespread power failures caused in part by a fire in a Pacific Gas and Electric Co. substation darkened entire neighborhoods of San Francisco from Saturday into Sunday, impacting roughly 130,000 homes and businesses — about one-third of all city customers served by the utility.

evidence.title: Over 7,000 SF Residents and Businesses Lost Power Monday Morning In Unplanned Outage
evidence.description: Upwards of 6,600 PG&E customers — representing well over 10,000 residents and businesses, if not closer to 20,000 — were without power Monday morning as PG&E deals with yet another unplanned outage.
snippets:
# Over 7,000 SF Residents and Businesses Lost Power Monday Morning In Unplanned Outage
Over 7,000 SF Residents and Businesses Lost Power Monday Morning In Unplanned Outage

Subsequently, PG&E said that the outage was continuing to impact "2,950 remaining customers" as of 12:40 pm, with the impact appearing to be concentrated in Corona Heights/Upper Market, several blocks of the Castro near Market Street, several blocks along Guerrero Street, and the 16th Street corridor.

The cause of the outage remains unclear, however for part of the Castro around Market, Noe, and Sanchez streets, this is repeat of a similar outage that took days to repair back in early July — impacting residents as well as bars that were trying to show World Cup matches.
